description: A fully synthetic TypeScript upload CLI development conversation. Project names, paths, hosts, IDs, commands, and test outputs are fictional narrative data. No model or production system was used to build this fixture.

content.text: We are working on Driftship, a TypeScript CLI for uploading a directory to a resumable HTTP object store. Add resumable parallel uploads. Read the repository first. The checkout is /work/driftship and the branch is feature/resumable-upload. Keep zero runtime dependencies and Node 22 or later. Initially I suggest six concurrent requests, eight-mebibyte chunks, and four retries, but inspect the server constraints before deciding. The existing command is driftship push <directory> --to <url>. This round is local development and tests. Do not publish, merge, or push anything to a remote.

I will trace enumeration, transport, and output first, then place the resume journal between scanning and upload execution. I will preserve the command shape and check the server protocol before finalizing defaults.

thread.output:
File: docs/server-protocol.md
# Object store protocol revision 3
The base URL contains a tenant prefix, for example https://storage.example.test/tenant-blue/.
Preserve the entire path. Object names use escaped path segments, not a single escaped slash-containing string. A percent character in a filename is literal and becomes %25. Do not normalize Unicode names.
GET capabilities returns protocol:3, minimum_chunk_bytes:1048576, maximum_chunk_bytes:16777216, preferred_chunk_bytes:4194304, maximum_parallel_parts:4, checksums:["sha256"].
POST uploads receives {path,size,chunk_bytes,sha256}; returns upload_id, expires_at, and committed_parts. Upload IDs are opaque, case-sensitive, and never local paths.
PUT uploads/{id}/parts/{part} has Content-Length, X-Part-SHA256, and binary body. Numbers are one-based. Only the last part may be short. Exact replay is idempotent for the same upload ID, part number, size, and checksum. Success returns 204, including identical replay. Different checksum returns 422/checksum_mismatch. A different body for an existing part returns 409/part_conflict.
GET uploads/{id} returns state open|complete|expired, part_size, file_size, file_sha256, and parts [{number,bytes,sha256}], potentially unordered. Complete state also has receipt. Missing session returns 404.
POST uploads/{id}/complete receives sorted parts and whole-file sha256. It atomically commits and returns {path,bytes,etag,sha256}. A lost success response can be reconciled by status; do not create a duplicate.
401/403 are permanent. 408,429,500,502,503,504 may be retried for idempotent PUTs. Retry-After may be delta seconds or an HTTP date. A connection may close after persisting a part. Authenticated writes do not support redirects. Administrative delete/abort endpoints are not part of ordinary client ownership.
Empty files use begin/complete with zero parts, SHA-256 of empty bytes, and no zero-byte part 1.
The proxy idle timeout is 90 seconds. Responses can arrive incrementally; consume the entire JSON body. JSON bodies are bounded to 1 MiB by the service. Capability discovery is authenticated like writes.

content.text: Use four workers and 4 MiB chunks, matching the server. Four retries means four extra attempts after the initial attempt. Put the journal at .driftship/resume-v1.json inside the source directory, with resume enabled by default. Add --no-resume to start fresh locally; it must not delete or abort remote sessions. Interrupted writes on removable drives matter, so make the journal durable.
I will use five total attempts with four retries, and one global pool of four requests. The journal will use temporary-file replacement with fsync. I will keep credentials out of state and output.

File: docs/operational-constraints.md
The token is read from DRIFTSHIP_TOKEN. Never serialize it into journals, progress, error output, or request snapshots. Reject redirects rather than forwarding authorization to another host.
JSON mode writes complete JSON objects one per stdout line. Human progress goes to stderr, final completion to stdout. Existing consumers use the type discriminator.
Median object size in the fixture corpus is 12 KiB. Bound active requests globally across the entire push, not separately per file. Do not launch one worker for every file.
Keep .git and .driftship excluded. Skip symlinks, FIFOs, and devices; do not follow targets or block on named pipes. Ordinary dotfiles are included. Filenames are data; a literal $(touch unexpected).txt must not run any command.
Two names café.csv and café.csv may be different filesystem entries. Preserve what Node reads. Do not guess normalization or deduplicate visually identical names.
Authentication is passed in a header, never URL userinfo. The source tree may contain shell hooks; this CLI never executes hooks from uploaded directories.
Empty files use no part requests. A receipt still counts as one completed file. Executable permission is recorded locally for diagnostics but not applied remotely: the service stores bytes, not Unix modes.

File: docs/resume.md
# Resume behavior
The journal lives inside the source at .driftship/resume-v1.json. Resume defaults on. --resume=off ignores old local state but does not delete remote sessions or objects. Server expiry owns cleanup.
Journal content: normalized destination identity, relative paths, size, nanosecond mtime, full SHA256, chunk size, opaque session IDs, confirmed parts, validated receipts. Credentials are absent. Parent0700 and file0600. Updates serialize, write temp, fsync file, rename, fsync directory. Disk failure is returned, never treated as success.
A full source hash is recomputed before reuse. Identity includes mtime as well as size/hash. Local match is insufficient: remote session size/hash/chunk also must match. Missing/expired remote sessions restart; inconsistent existing sessions fail.
Do not modify the source tree during transfer. Driftship detects many changes before hashing and before complete, but offers no atomic snapshot or locks. A race remains between final verification and completion.
Only exact PUT part replay retries. Begin/complete do not. Ambiguous complete connection loss allows one status read. Matching complete receipt succeeds; status failure is surfaced. The next invocation reconciles remote committed parts.
Ctrl-C stops scheduling, aborts in-flight requests, settles queued journal writes, exits130. It never deletes sessions.
Durability has been exercised on Linux only. Windows directory-fsync and rename semantics are unvalidated. A filesystem rejecting directory sync returns an I/O error. Do not advertise Windows durability before platform tests.
Error codes:1 server/transport/local I/O;2 usage/config;3 invalid journal or destination/session mismatch;130 interruption. Server checksum failures are1.

facts.statement: Driftship is a Node 22+ TypeScript CLI with no runtime dependencies.
No push, merge, or package publication is authorized.
Protocol 3 advertises preferred chunks 4194304 bytes and maximum four parallel parts.
Object URLs retain the tenant path, encode segments individually, and preserve Unicode spelling.
Part replay is idempotent only for the same upload ID, part number, length, and checksum.
Final defaults are four global workers, 4 MiB chunks, four extra retries/five total attempts.
Journal is .driftship/resume-v1.json and resume defaults on.
Empty files have no part requests and use SHA-256 of empty bytes.
Scanner excludes .git/.driftship, skips symlinks/FIFOs/devices, and includes ordinary dotfiles.
Global concurrency bounds the entire push rather than each file independently.
Local identity uses full SHA-256, size, and nanosecond mtime.
Destination rejects query/fragment/userinfo without echoing secrets; only trailing slash normalization is allowed.
JournalStore serializes mutations and later queued operations retain the first write failure.
Journal replacement uses mode0600 temp file, file fsync, rename, parent-directory fsync; parent is0700.
Dry-run sends no network requests and creates no .driftship directory.
Begin/complete POSTs do not retry; one status GET is allowed for ambiguous complete failure.
Stale-session deletion was brainstorming, explicitly not approved.
Receipt validation checks path, bytes, SHA-256, and nonempty etag.
Eight focused recovery tests passed after completion reconciliation was fixed.
